ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Year-one academic inquiry, writing and civic engagement.
ACCPPDE101.topics: Scholarly sources and research questions; Argumentation and thesis statements; Literature synthesis; Academic integrity and referencing; Community engagement; Personal learning goals and reflective learning; Collaborative learning; Self-efficacy; Stress and time management; Responsible use of AI
ACCPPDE101.methods: Scholarly literature searching and source evaluation; Literature synthesis; CARS model for research introductions; Reflective development planning; Community project co-design

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design
BENENTR111.contribution: teaches the design and development cycle in a team (interviewing customers, forming a product concept, developing a fabrication method, analysing costs and sustainability) with experiments, mathematical modelling and prototyping; it directly implements the team design-and-development cycle of the design project lines, although the products are consumer products and not clinical applications
BENENTR111.topics: Consumer needs; Product concepts and specifications; Product working mechanisms; Prototyping; Laboratory-to-industrial production scaling; Materials and resource use; Product lifespan, repairability and circularity; Environmental impact; Production costs and commercial viability
BENENTR111.methods: Consumer interviews; Needs ranking and specification development; Concept-criteria matrices; Quantitative product modelling; Product investigation and experimentation; Prototyping; Process-flow diagrams and material balances; Environmental-impact estimation; Break-even analysis

BENENTR311.name: Market Research
BENENTR311.contribution: teaches how to plan and carry out customer and market research, analyse the findings and turn them into business ideas; it makes a specific complementary contribution to testing the market value of an innovation, but it is not specific to health care
BENENTR311.topics: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas. Ready to turn curiosity into career skills? Perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.contribution: teaches venture creation from ideation to pitch with design thinking, business-model development, market validation and business planning; it directly implements the entrepreneurship and market-value part of the curriculum (From Research to Market Value and the valorisation aims of the design project), without any health-care content
BENGATE101.topics: Entrepreneurial mindset and pathways; Business environments, ownership and competition; Customer needs; Value propositions; Business models; Marketing and sales; Finance and accounting; Venture funding; Operations and human resources; Competitive positioning; Startup growth and business lifecycles; Sustainability and societal impact
BENGATE101.methods: Design thinking; Customer-needs discovery; Ideation and prototyping; Value Proposition Canvas; Business Model Canvas; Business planning; SWOT and risk assessment; Startup simulation

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: teaches research design, operationalisation, sampling, experiments and surveys and descriptive and inferential statistics including analysis of variance; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the experimental design, statistics and reporting of experimental data in the lab skills lines and to research training for the thesis, although it is oriented to business and behavioural research
BENGATE102.topics: Scientific inquiry and hypotheses; Operationalization and measurement; Reliability and validity; Survey construction and sampling; Randomized and quasi-experimental designs; Nonexperimental and qualitative research; Descriptive statistics; Sampling distributions and estimation; Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals; Association and regression; Research ethics and anonymous data collection
BENGATE102.methods: Survey design; Probability and nonprobability sampling; Experimental and nonexperimental research design; R and R Commander data analysis; Descriptive statistics and visualization; Scale-reliability analysis; One- and two-sample mean tests; ANOVA; Chi-square tests; Correlation and regression; Empirical data collection and analysis

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: develops data visualisation, cleaning and manipulation on real data sets and ends with an own research project; it directly implements the data-handling, visualisation and analysis part of Coding and Data Crunching
DISDATA111.topics: Data visualization; Exploratory data analysis; Tidy data; Data transformation and integration; Dates and times; Web data; Text data; Geospatial data; Programming functions; Data-based research questions
DISDATA111.methods: R programming; ggplot visualization and grammar of graphics; Data cleaning, tidying and transformation; Data import and joins; Web scraping; Text-data analysis; Geospatial-data analysis

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.contribution: Trains predictive modelling, resampling, classification, regularisation and tree methods. These are transferable data-driven methods for biosystem modelling.
DISDATA211.topics: Prediction and model accuracy; Regression and classification; Resampling and validation; Model selection and regularization; High-dimensional data; Nonlinear regression; Tree-based learning; Support vector methods; Dimension reduction; Unsupervised learning; Feature engineering
DISDATA211.methods: Linear and logistic regression; Generative classification; Cross-validation and bootstrap; Subset selection; Ridge regression and LASSO; Splines and generalized additive models; Basic and advanced decision-tree methods; Support vector machines; Principal component analysis; Clustering; Predictive-performance evaluation; R or Python implementation

DISGATE101.name: Introduction to Programming
DISGATE101.contribution: introduces structured and object-oriented programming in Python with testing and debugging and computational problem-solving; it directly implements the scripting and programming foundation of Coding and Data Crunching, which uses R
DISGATE101.topics: Python language fundamentals; Strings and input/output; Branching and loops; Functions; Tuples, lists, sets and dictionaries; Aliasing and cloning; Recursion; Exceptions and assertions; Object-oriented programming; Inheritance; Computational problem-solving
DISGATE101.methods: Structured programming in Python; Object-oriented programming; Recursive problem-solving; Program tracing; Testing and debugging; Exception handling

DISGATE102.name: Mathematical Methods
DISGATE102.contribution: teaches integration, complex numbers, differential equations and equation solving; it directly implements the mathematics of differential equations and integration used in Foundations of Engineering and Data Analysis & Modelling of Biosystems
DISGATE102.topics: Functions and limits; Continuity; Differentiation; Optimization; Taylor series; Complex numbers; Definite and indefinite integrals; Integration techniques; First-order differential equations; Population-growth and predator–prey models; Second-order linear differential equations; Dynamic models
DISGATE102.methods: Analytical differentiation and integration; Taylor approximation; Newton's method; Numerical integration; Euler's method; Analytical solution of differential equations; Computer algebra with Mathematica; Dynamic-model implementation and analysis

DISMATH213.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
DISMATH213.contribution: teaches numerical methods for differential equations, root finding, interpolation, differentiation and integration with attention to accuracy and stability; it directly implements the differential-equation modelling and simulation of Data Analysis & Modelling of Biosystems, but without biological applications
DISMATH213.topics: Computer arithmetic and roundoff; Algorithm convergence and error; Scalar root finding; Polynomial interpolation and splines; Parametric curves; Numerical differentiation and integration; Initial-value problems; Multistep and adaptive differential-equation methods; Stability and stiff equations; Linear systems and matrix factorization; Nonlinear systems; Numerical-result validation
DISMATH213.methods: Mathematica numerical computation; Bisection, fixed-point, Newton and secant methods; Polynomial and spline interpolation; Numerical differentiation and Richardson extrapolation; Simpson, Romberg and Gaussian quadrature; Adaptive quadrature; Euler and Runge-Kutta methods; Multistep predictor-corrector methods; Gaussian elimination and pivoting; Matrix factorizations; Newton and quasi-Newton methods for systems; Steepest descent; Continuation methods

DISMATH314.name: Probability & Statistics
DISMATH314.contribution: provides the foundation of mathematical statistics: probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; it directly implements the probability and statistics taught in Coding and Data Crunching at greater mathematical depth
DISMATH314.topics: Probability spaces and conditional probability; Random variables and expectation; Moment-generating functions; Discrete and continuous distributions; Multivariate and conditional distributions; Transformations and correlation; Sampling and order statistics; Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests; Estimation efficiency; Bayesian inference; Monte Carlo methods
DISMATH314.methods: Analytical probability calculation; Maximum-likelihood estimation and testing; Chi-square tests; Bootstrap; EM algorithm; Bayesian updating; Inverse-transform sampling; Accept-reject sampling; Gibbs sampling; Monte Carlo simulation in Mathematica

ENSGATE101.name: Sustainability Essentials I
ENSGATE101.contribution: provides key concepts in physics, chemistry, materials science, mathematics and modelling and applies them to a case study; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the physics, mathematics and materials foundations of Foundations of Engineering, although it is framed for sustainability and not for human biomechanics
ENSGATE101.topics: Planetary boundaries and the Anthropocene; Exponential growth and environmental change; Graphs, rates and uncertainty; Dynamic systems; Chemical bonds, reactions and equilibria; Ocean acidification and nutrient cycles; Thermodynamics and entropy; Greenhouse gases and energy; Ozone depletion; Newtonian mechanics, stress and strain; Biopolymers and material properties
ENSGATE101.methods: Graph interpretation and comparison; Fermi estimation; Difference-equation and first-order linear differential-equation modelling; Elementary differentiation and integration; Biopolymer preparation; Strength and elasticity measurement; Iterative experimental improvement

ENSGATE201.name: Sustainability Essentials II
ENSGATE201.contribution: builds on Sustainability Essentials I with three topics, waves, chemistry and materials science, and a project that applies them; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the chemistry and materials-science foundations behind Materials Science in Biological Applications, but it is a sustainability course and teaches no biomaterials or cell-material interaction
ENSGATE201.topics: Electromagnetic and mechanical waves; Wave composition and interference; Optical spectroscopy; Electron microscopy; Inorganic and organic chemistry; Chemical testing; Material structure and crystallography; Stress and strain; Sustainable material design; Geological wave applications; Nuclear power and waste; Greenwashing
ENSGATE201.methods: Oscilloscope wave visualization; Optical-spectroscopy interpretation; Fourier wave analysis; Copper dissolution and chemical analysis; Laboratory logbook documentation; Stress-strain analysis; Mohr's-circle application; Evidence-based greenwashing case analysis; Public sustainability-communication design

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: teaches moral-reasoning theories and practical ethics including privacy, equality and future generations; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the ethical debate on regenerative-medicine applications in Regenerative Medicine in Society and to the ethical and integrity standards of the academic development lines, but it has no biomedical focus
GOSPHIL212.topics: Divine command and human nature; Moral relativism and universalism; Utilitarianism and consequentialism; Kantian ethics; Virtue ethics; Social contract and intuitionism; Feminist and care ethics; Nietzschean genealogy and nihilism; Murdoch's sovereignty of good; Moral value and perspective; Death, absurdity and meaning; Ethical theory and practical judgment

HCBBIOM211.name: Functional Anatomy
HCBBIOM211.contribution: studies the structure of the human body in relation to function through imaging, surface anatomy and dissection materials, system by system; it directly implements the anatomy taught in Principles of Medicine
HCBBIOM211.topics: Anatomical terminology and body planes; Medical imaging; Skeletal system and vertebral column; Thorax and pelvis; Respiratory and cardiovascular systems; Abdominal organs and vascular supply; Reproductive and lower urinary systems; Anatomical variation and intersex presentations; Human remains and dissection ethics; History and representation of the body
HCBBIOM211.methods: Surface-anatomy observation; Anatomical image interpretation; Scientific anatomical drawing; Three-dimensional anatomical reasoning; Guided study of human skeletal remains and anatomical specimens; Ethical reflection on anatomical practice

HCBBIOM311.name: Pharmacology
HCBBIOM311.contribution: covers the origin, kinetics, targets, therapeutic use and toxicity of drugs and explains therapies through molecular targets and physiological consequences; it makes a specific complementary contribution to understanding the medicinal and advanced-therapy treatments that regenerative approaches complement or replace, but it contains no regenerative-medicine content
HCBBIOM311.topics: Drug discovery and targets; Drug-receptor interactions; Pharmacodynamics; Absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination; Pharmacokinetics; Antimicrobial therapy; Inflammation and immunopharmacology; Autonomic regulation; Neurotransmission and psychoactive drugs; Pharmacogenomics; Drug toxicity; Access to experimental treatments and evidence; Homeopathy
HCBBIOM311.methods: Concentration-response modelling; Pharmacokinetic time-concentration and time-response analysis; Pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic parameter calculation; Virtual organ-bath experiments; Hypothesis and experimental-design development

HCBBIOM312.name: Infection & Immunity
HCBBIOM312.contribution: teaches innate and adaptive immune responses, recognition of self and non-self, inflammation, tissue damage and immunopathology; it directly implements the immunology and inflammation taught in Principles of Medicine and the immune interactions that Technological Trends in Regenerative Medicine applies to implants and cell therapies, although it is not taught in a transplant or regeneration context
HCBBIOM312.topics: Infectious agents and microbial virulence; Host defence and immune evasion; Immune cells, organs and cytokines; Innate immunity and complement; Antibodies and antigen recognition; MHC and lymphocyte receptors; Lymphocyte activation, development and memory; Cell- and antibody-mediated immunity; Mucosal immunity; Vaccination and viral infections; Hypersensitivity and allergy; Immunodeficiency; Autoimmune disease; Outbreak management

HCBBIOM313.name: Mechanisms of Disease
HCBBIOM313.contribution: Examines organ-system pathology and treatment, including renal failure, dialysis and transplantation. It supplies clinical context for regeneration and alternatives to transplantation.
HCBBIOM313.topics: Organ-system disease mechanisms; Nutrition and digestive disease; Hematological and cardiovascular disease; Respiratory disease; Renal failure, dialysis and transplantation; Endocrine disorders; Neurological disease; Etiology and pathogenesis; Diagnosis, treatment and prognosis; Medical ethics; Rheumatic disease

HCBGATE101.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
HCBGATE101.contribution: introduces biochemistry, macromolecules, cells, organ systems, DNA and cell function and connects them to health and disease; it directly implements the biological foundation that The Molecular Basis of Life and Principles of Medicine build on, without their regenerative-medicine framing
HCBGATE101.topics: Biological molecules and chemistry of life; Cells, organelles and membranes; Cellular communication; Enzymes and energy metabolism; Cell cycle and division; DNA and heredity; Gene mutation and molecular medicine; Gene-expression regulation and epigenetics; Genomes; Recombinant DNA and biotechnology

HCBLIFE211.contribution: Develops molecular cell biology through signalling, cell division, tissue organisation, cell fate and stem cells. This supplies foundations for regenerative cell biology and cell-production study.
HCBLIFE211.topics: Cellular components and bioenergetics; Proteins and membranes; Cytoskeleton; DNA replication and repair; Genomes; Regulation of gene expression; Membrane transport and trafficking; Cell-signalling pathways; Cell division and fate; Tissue organization; Stem cells; Cancer; Molecular mechanisms of drug action
HCBLIFE211.methods: Critical analysis of primary molecular-biology literature; Evaluation of research-method limitations and reproducibility; Thermodynamic free-energy calculations; Molecular mechanism analysis

HCBLIFE212.name: Human Physiology
HCBLIFE212.contribution: studies the normal functioning of the human body, from molecular and cellular physiology through homeostasis and signalling to the integration of organ systems; it directly implements the physiology taught in Principles of Medicine
HCBLIFE212.topics: Cells, tissues and membrane dynamics; Homeostasis and control; Cellular signalling; Endocrine and nervous regulation; Muscles and movement; Breathing and gas exchange; Blood and cardiovascular function; Renal function; Fluid and electrolyte balance; Digestion and metabolism; Growth and exercise physiology; Reproduction and development

HCBLIFE213.name: Biochemistry
HCBLIFE213.contribution: explores the chemistry of life, namely proteins, sugars, lipids and nucleic acids, metabolic pathways and applications in medicine and biotechnology; it directly implements the biomolecular and chemical part of The Molecular Basis of Life, but it is biochemistry rather than the general, organic and physical chemistry that course also teaches
HCBLIFE213.topics: Water and weak bonds; Amino acids and protein structure; Protein-biochemistry techniques; Enzyme action, kinetics, regulation and inhibition; Hemoglobin; Carbohydrates and lipids; Metabolic organization; Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis; Citric-acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation; Glycogen and pentose-phosphate metabolism; Fatty-acid and lipid metabolism; Nitrogen and urea cycle; Biochemical mechanisms of disease

HCBLIFE214.name: Life Science Laboratory
HCBLIFE214.contribution: introduces biochemical and molecular laboratory work on blood, bacteria, protein production and analysis, DNA isolation and bioinformatics searches and builds a foundation for biomedical research; it directly implements part of the laboratory training in the lab skills lines, although its themes do not include stem-cell culture or biomaterials work
HCBLIFE214.topics: Blood cells and proteins; Blood groups and hemograms; Aseptic culture and bacterial identification; Disinfection and sterilization; Antibiotic susceptibility; Genetically modified bacteria; GFP production and purification; DNA and plasmid analysis; PCR and restriction digestion; Protein and DNA databases; Genotype and population-genetic interpretation; Experimental reproducibility

HCBLIFE311.contribution: Studies cell injury, inflammation, tissue repair, regeneration and fibrosis, plus gene-based therapies and cell manipulation. It directly supports the biological study of repair and parts of advanced therapy.
HCBLIFE311.topics: Cell injury, adaptation and death; Acute and chronic inflammation; Regeneration, repair and fibrosis; Neoplasia; Pulmonary pathology; Leukemia and lymphoma; Genes, genomes and inheritance; Genetic variation and chromosome abnormalities; Gene regulation and epigenetics; Genotype-phenotype relationships; Genetic testing and DNA technologies; Gene-based therapies and cell manipulation; Genetics ethics, law and biosafety

analysis: The closest plan develops cell structure, stem cells, molecular and cellular physiology, organ function, anatomy, immunology, pharmacology and pathology. Molecular pathology supplies direct tissue repair, fibrosis and gene-therapy content. Life Science Laboratory includes aseptic culture, PCR and protein purification, but does not supply the advanced regenerative laboratory sequence. Renal disease, dialysis and transplantation give concrete organ-replacement context. The two sustainability courses supply mechanics, materials structure, stress and strain, spectroscopy and chemistry. Computing, mathematical modelling and statistics develop modelling and data analysis transferable to biosystems. Product design provides requirements, prototyping and evaluation of materials and manufacturing costs. The ventures and market research courses address customer validation and translation, and ethics adds general normative reasoning. Considered a device focus using Robotics (kinematics, motion planning, sensors), Linear Systems (signals, filtering, feedback), physiology, anatomy, modelling and consumer product design. These are genuine engineering contributions but the clinically specific device design, biomechanics and validation sequence remains too thin to support a distinct second programme. For biomaterials and tissue engineering, considered the course descriptions and outlines for materials properties, characterization, polymer study, cell fate and stem cells. They support foundational science but do not establish scaffold design, biomaterial–cell interaction or fabrication of living tissues. Consumer Product Design moves to Spring 2029 and Research Methods & Statistics to Spring 2028, preserving all selections and improving the research preparation timing. The clinical design comparison explicitly retains the difference in application. The optional UCR independent research row is outside 180 EC.

alignment.rationale: Both study the molecular basis of life. UCR focuses on proteins, metabolism and biochemical techniques. Maastricht also uses chemistry and cell biology to introduce regenerative medicine.
Both develop cell biology, including cell fate and stem cells. Maastricht extends this to cell sourcing, manufacture and cell–material constructs.
Both develop molecular laboratory skills. Maastricht also integrates lab practice across its first-year courses.
Maastricht awards 2 EC for meeting the first-year laboratory attendance requirement.
Maastricht continues lab training in cell culture, assays and materials. UCR develops related laboratory foundations in its life science lab.
Maastricht awards 2 EC for meeting the second-year laboratory attendance requirement.
Both study organ function and physiology. Maastricht combines physiology with anatomy and immunology in the same course.
Both examine immune responses relevant to regenerative treatments. Maastricht also studies therapies and devices, including implants and cell-based treatments.
Both study tissue repair and regeneration. Maastricht concentrates on the regenerative capacity of different tissues and the factors that limit it.
Maastricht introduces regenerative medicine and its applications in society. UCR covers related biology and general ethics across separate courses.
Both develop quantitative and physical foundations. UCR includes mechanics and material properties in sustainability contexts. Maastricht also teaches engineering tools for biomechanics.
UCR studies material properties and characterisation in sustainability. Maastricht focuses on biomaterials and their interaction with cells.
Maastricht teaches specialist methods such as microfabrication, microfluidics, organs-on-chips and biofabrication.
Both use programming to explore and analyse data. Maastricht’s course combines R scripting and statistics in regenerative-medicine examples.
Both develop data-driven models. Maastricht combines these with differential equations and examples from biological systems.
Both develop and test product concepts in teams. Maastricht uses a clinical regeneration problem. UCR uses consumer products.
Both explore how ideas become marketable products. Maastricht focuses on the value of regenerative-medicine research. UCR teaches general venture design and validation.
Maastricht introduces the design process through interviews, journal clubs, visits and a project pitch.
Both develop academic, communication and reflective skills. Maastricht continues its academic development sequence throughout the year.
Maastricht continues its academic development sequence and prepares students for their minor and graduation project.
Students complete a 30 EC minor. Choices can include courses at Maastricht or another university, with approval where required.
Maastricht’s 30 EC graduation project combines an internship, an individual thesis and an oral defence. UCR’s optional independent research is outside the scheduled plan.
